# Which direction did the couple in black coats come from?

## Short answer

They came **from the left of the frame — from the near, left-hand (foreground) end of the railed walkway**, and they are continuing **to the right and away from the camera**, deeper into the cave. If this were a video, you would have seen them enter at the left edge of the shot, relatively large and close to the camera, and walk rightwards while steadily shrinking as the path carried them back into the chamber, arriving at the spot where they are now.

## What the scene shows

The photograph is the interior of a show cave: a densely "strawed" ceiling of thin soda-straw stalactites above, big lit flowstone columns on the right, and a metal-railed visitor walkway crossing the lower-left portion of the frame. Four visitors are on that walkway. The two nearest the camera, on the left, are a person in a bright orange/red jacket and a person in an olive/tan coat. Beyond them, further to the right, are the two figures asked about: a pair in long dark/black coats.

## Evidence for the direction of travel

**1. We are looking at the couple's backs, not their faces.** Enlarged and brightened, both black-coated figures resolve as pure back views: no facial features are recoverable on either, while the olive-coated person nearer the camera clearly shows a lit face at the same exposure. The right-hand figure of the couple shows the back of a head with longer hair spreading onto the shoulders. Because their backs are to the lens, they are facing *into* the scene, i.e. away from the camera — so they are heading away, not approaching.

**2. The walkway recedes from lower-left to upper-right, so "away" means "to the right".** Measured in the original 3888 × 2592 file, the four visitors' apparent heights fall off monotonically from left to right: roughly 596 px (orange jacket), 546 px (olive coat), 504 px (left member of the couple), 446 px (right member of the couple). Over the same span the handrail rises in the frame, the railing uprights get shorter, and the spacing between uprights shrinks from about 100 px to about 60–70 px. All of this says one continuous walkway running obliquely away from the camera towards the right. The couple are the two furthest along it.

**3. The other two visitors are walking the same way, which fixes the flow of traffic.** At high magnification the orange-jacketed person's face appears on the *right-hand* side of their head (head bowed, watching the path), their leading foot is planted forward and to the right at about x = 241–305 px while their trailing foot is behind them off to the left at about x < 80 px. That is an unambiguous left-to-right stride. The olive-coated person is likewise mid-stride with the leading shoe placed to the right, head turned outwards toward the formations as they walk. So the whole group is moving left → right, and the couple in black — being the furthest right — are simply the ones furthest along that same route.

**4. Stride cues on the couple agree.** The right-hand black-coated figure has one pale-trousered leg planted and the other foot lifted clear of the deck behind it, and their arm is extended forward and to the right along the handrail — a walking posture, not a stationary one. The left-hand figure has their feet noticeably apart, consistent with being in step behind their partner.

**5. Where they are heading.** Just to the right of them, in the middle distance, the handrail bends around a rounded, curving railed section — the far end of this stretch of walkway, where it turns and the lit path passes out of the frame into the dark beyond the big illuminated columns. That is ahead of them, not behind them.

## Putting it as a video

Run the clip backwards and the couple would walk leftwards, growing larger in the frame, passing behind (and then in front of) the olive-coated and orange-jacketed visitors, and exit past the left edge of the picture at the near end of the walkway. Run it forwards from the captured instant and they continue to the right, getting smaller, towards the curved railing and the bend where the path turns away.

## Directions they did *not* come from

- **Not from the right.** The right-hand end of this walkway is the bend they are still walking towards; and if they had come from there they would be walking back towards the camera and we would be seeing their faces, not their backs.
- **Not from behind the camera / out of the foreground.** There is open cave floor with lit stalagmites between the camera position and the near railing, so the camera is not standing on this section of walkway; the only way onto the couple's stretch of path within this view is along it, from the left.

criteria.justification: The candidate states they came "from the left of the frame" and would continue rightwards.

Answer: The couple in the black coats came from the LEFT side of the frame (the lower-left foreground, near the camera). They are walking toward the RIGHT and away from the camera, deeper into the cave, so in a video they would have entered from the left and moved rightward to reach their current position.

Reasoning, stated explicitly:

1. Where they are. The couple stands on the railed tourist walkway in the lower-middle of the picture, just to the right of a small lit stalagmite. The walkway runs from the lower-left corner of the image (the end closest to the camera) toward the right and slightly upward into the distance, where the paved path surface and a second, farther railing are visible on the right side. So the only two possible travel directions along this path are "from the left toward the right/background" or "from the right/background toward the left/foreground."

2. Which way they face. Both people in black coats are seen from behind. The taller person on the left shows only the back of a dark hooded coat; the hood sits at the back of the neck and no face, cheek, or chin is visible. The person on the right shows long dark hair hanging straight down over the collar and shoulders, again with no face visible. For comparison, the two other visitors farther left on the same walkway (one in an orange-red jacket, one in a brown/olive coat) are turned toward the left and their faces are clearly lit and visible in profile under the same cave lighting. If the couple were also facing left, their faces would be lit and visible in the same way. They are not, so the couple is facing right, with their backs to the camera.

3. Gait. Both people in black are mid-stride with their legs apart, so they are walking rather than standing. The person on the right (in light jeans) has the rear foot planted on the ground at the lower-left and the other foot lifted; the lifted foot joins the leg at its lower-left end (the heel/ankle) and its toe points up and to the right, i.e., in the direction of travel along the path away from the camera. This matches a forward step toward the right.

4. Conclusion. Because the couple is walking rightward and away from the viewer along the walkway, they must have come from the left side of the frame: the lower-left, camera-near end of the walkway where the orange-jacket and brown-coat visitors are now. They are moving in the opposite direction to those two visitors, who are walking leftward toward the camera-side end of the path. In short: the couple traveled from the left (foreground-left) to reach their current spot, and they are heading to the right (background).
